Summarize and Print a Bayesian PCA Imputation

Source: R/mi_pca_s3.R
summary.si_mi.Rd

summary() returns Rhat and ESS for a sample of the missing values of a fit. print() shows a fit or a summary.

Usage

# S3 method for class 'si_mi_pca'
print(x, ...)

# S3 method for class 'si_mi'
print(x, ...)

# S3 method for class 'si_mi_pca'
summary(object, prop_diag = 0.5, ...)

# S3 method for class 'si_mi'
summary(object, ...)

# S3 method for class 'si_mi_summary'
print(x, n = 6L, ...)

Arguments

x

A si_mi, si_mi_pca or si_mi_summary object.

...

Not used.

object

A si_mi or si_mi_pca object. A fit from mipca() or mipca_fit().

prop_diag

Numeric scalar between 0 and 1. Proportion of each column's missing values on which Rhat and ESS are computed. 0 is refused. Only a resumable fit takes it. Defaults to 0.5.

n

Integer. Number of values with the highest Rhat to list. 0 lists none. Defaults to 6.

Value

  • summary(): an object of class si_mi_summary. Its attributes prop_diag, nchains and ndraws hold the proportion, the number of chains and the draws per chain, or NA where joined fits differ. Its element cells is a data frame with one row per value, in column order:

    • chunk: the fit the value comes from, 1 unless fits were joined with cbind(). Finalized fits only.

    • col, name: the column number and name in the completed matrix.

    • row: the row number.

    • rhat, ess: Rhat and ESS.

  • print(): x, invisibly.

Details

Rhat and ESS. Rhat is the folded split Rhat of Vehtari et al. (2021). ESS is computed over all chains together. update() adds draws to a resumable fit, which raises ESS.

Which values. A column with h missing values gives ceiling(prop_diag * h) of them, spread evenly along the column. The sample is the same on every call. Columns listed in abb are left out.

Finalized and resumable fits. A finalized fit returns the values computed when it was finalized, with the prop_diag given to mipca() or mipca_finalize(). A resumable fit computes them on each call, with the prop_diag given here.

Short runs. Rhat is NA with fewer than 4 draws per chain, and ESS is NA with fewer than 12.

Joined fits. For fits joined with cbind(), chunk gives the fit each value comes from. print() shows mixed where the fits differ in prop_diag, chains or draws.

Printing. print() of a fit shows its size and the calls to make next. print() of a summary shows the number of values, the quantiles of rhat and ess, and the n values with the highest Rhat.

References

Vehtari A, Gelman A, Simpson D, Carpenter B, Burkner P-C (2021). Rank-normalization, folding, and localization: an improved R-hat for assessing convergence of MCMC. Bayesian Analysis, 16(2), 667-718. doi:10.1214/20-BA1221

See also

  • mipca() to fit, and choose prop_diag.

  • update() to add draws to a resumable fit.

Examples

set.seed(1)
sim <- sim_mat(n = 50, p = 20, beta = TRUE)
fit <- mipca(sim$input, rank = 2, transform = "logit_biwhiten", seed = 1)
s <- summary(fit)
s
#> si_mi_summary: Rhat and ESS for 50 cells in 10 columns
#>   prop_diag 0.5, 4 chains x 100 draws
#>           0% 25%    50%    75%   100%
#> rhat   0.996   1   1.01   1.01   1.03
#> ess  153.000 291 330.00 354.00 409.00
#> worst 6 cells by rhat:
#>  chunk col      name row     rhat      ess
#>      1  10 feature10  11 1.029468 230.5473
#>      1   7  feature7   4 1.017100 333.5527
#>      1  14 feature14   2 1.016376 348.8917
#>      1  10 feature10  28 1.016294 219.3950
#>      1  20 feature20   5 1.016222 266.4496
#>      1  15 feature15  35 1.015993 300.7472
print(s, n = 3)
#> si_mi_summary: Rhat and ESS for 50 cells in 10 columns
#>   prop_diag 0.5, 4 chains x 100 draws
#>           0% 25%    50%    75%   100%
#> rhat   0.996   1   1.01   1.01   1.03
#> ess  153.000 291 330.00 354.00 409.00
#> worst 3 cells by rhat:
#>  chunk col      name row     rhat      ess
#>      1  10 feature10  11 1.029468 230.5473
#>      1   7  feature7   4 1.017100 333.5527
#>      1  14 feature14   2 1.016376 348.8917
head(s$cells)
#>   chunk col     name row     rhat      ess
#> 1     1   3 feature3   3 1.001578 377.5531
#> 2     1   3 feature3  13 1.007004 378.1096
#> 3     1   3 feature3  19 1.014247 291.7192
#> 4     1   3 feature3  38 1.000465 328.7449
#> 5     1   3 feature3  49 1.005982 322.9542
#> 6     1   4 feature4   8 1.011456 234.8404

# A resumable fit takes prop_diag at each call
fit <- mipca(sim$input, rank = 2, transform = "logit_biwhiten", keep_state = TRUE, seed = 1)
summary(fit, prop_diag = 1)
#> si_mi_summary: Rhat and ESS for 100 cells in 10 columns
#>   prop_diag 1, 4 chains x 100 draws
#>           0% 25%    50%    75%   100%
#> rhat   0.994   1   1.01   1.01   1.03
#> ess  153.000 290 323.00 354.00 442.00
#> worst 6 cells by rhat:
#>  col      name row     rhat      ess
#>   10 feature10  11 1.029468 230.5473
#>    7  feature7  46 1.023850 168.3942
#>   17 feature17  26 1.018449 278.6523
#>    7  feature7   4 1.017100 333.5527
#>   14 feature14   2 1.016376 348.8917
#>   10 feature10  28 1.016294 219.3950
